correctness.rationale: The final claim assumes r_n=n^{alpha+o(1)}, m_n=n^{beta+o(1)}, alpha,beta>0, fixed p in (0,1) and independence of entries INSIDE each matrix, without cross-index independence. For k=floor((1-epsilon)log r/lambda), every k-attribute subset has Bin(r,p^k) support, mean at least r^epsilon. Conditional independence of outside columns gives closure-failure <=exp(-r^epsilon/8)+m exp(-lambda r^epsilon/2); union over m^k=exp(O(log^2 n)) makes failures summable. The lower bound log binom(m,k)~(1-epsilon)log r log m/lambda follows. A concept with extent >=A=ceil((1+epsilon)log m/lambda) and intent >=B=ceil((1+epsilon)log r/lambda) induces a distinct all-one rectangle. Its first-moment sum is <=rm exp(A log r+B log m-lambda AB), with high-high exponent <=(1-epsilon^2)log r log m/lambda+O(log n); Markov plus Borel-Cantelli and smaller-side deterministic counts prove the upper a.s. and expectation bounds. The argument needs no independence across n. Independently computed all incidence matrices at p=1/2 for 2x2,3x3,4x4, obtaining expectations 39/16,1977/512,386463/65536; these are checks, not a substitute for the universal argument.
